newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Air NZ details complex Ansett purchase plan.
newsitem.headline: Air NZ details complex Ansett purchase plan.

text.p: Air New Zealand Ltd on Monday released details of a complex funding package for the A$475 millon (US$375.0 million) purchase of TNT Ltd's half share in Ansett Airlines
The cimplicated deal involves a cash issue, new borrowings and existing cash reserves.
Simultaneously, the New Zealand Government said it would relax foreign ownership provisions of Air NZ.
Air NZ earlier reported a 13.4 percent decline in profit to NZ$225.2 million, the company's second highest profit.
Directors said it would be difficult to match that outcome in the current year. Analysts said this went some way to explain Air NZ's need for Ansett if it wanted to keep on growing.
Australia's Foreign Investment Review Board is still considering Air NZ's application for Ansett and a decision is due this month.
If approval is granted, it will end a long-running saga that started two years ago when then Prime Minister Paul Keating shot down a single aviation agreement with New Zealand.
The on-again off-again deal has gone through several permutations, the latest meaning Ansett's New Zealand operations will not be part of the transaction.
Air NZ chairman Bob Matthew said it was a strategic move into the Australasian regional aviation market.

"By owning half of Ansett Australia's domestic airline business and a significant interest in its international business, Air NZ will secure immediate, low-risk and cost-effective participation in the Australian domestic market and wider access to international origin markets through coordination of complementary services," he said.

The total sum involved is made up of a purchase price of A$133 million; loans of A$122 million by Air NZ to Ansett to repay TNT's subordinated debt in Ansett; subscription of A$70 million for redeemable preference shares in Ansett to replace those held by TNT; additional capital contribution by Air NZ to Ansett of A$150 million, together with a further A$50 million capital contribution by News Ltd
News owns the other half of Ansett.
Air NZ said it would fund the purchase with about NZ$350 million of existing cash reserves and NZ$190 million of new borrowings.
It also expects to raise about NZ$240 million through a three-for-eleven rights issue at NZ$2.00/share.
In a separate development, the New Zealand Government granted Air NZ permission to raise the proportion of "B" shares, which can be held by foreign investors, to 49 percent from 35 percent.

The directors said they had been aware for some time of an imbalance in demand for the two types of shares and the lack of liquidity in the "B" shares had constrained the market prices of both securities.
The B shares last traded at NZ$4.33, a subtantial premium to the A shares, which traded at $3.14.
